messages:
ashley: Heads-up — saw a sharp p99 tail during tenant compaction + recovery in staging this morning. Looks like pages that are being rehydrated keep getting evicted by the local evictor and retried, causing a thundering-wheel of demote/rehydrate. proposing a lightweight handshake between evictor <-> tenant-manager to avoid thrash. sketch below.

sam: Can you paste the logs/repro? wondering if it's the eviction policy or a bug in residency tracking.

ashley: logs:
```
[2026-04-07T09:12:03Z] evictor: evict page p-42 tenant=t-7 decision=ok
[2026-04-07T09:12:03Z] rehydration: start page p-42 tenant=t-7 src=host
[2026-04-07T09:12:03Z] evictor: evict page p-42 tenant=t-7 decision=ok
[2026-04-07T09:12:04Z] rehydration: retry page p-42 tenant=t-7 delay=10ms
```
And a tiny proto of the handshake I sketched:
```py
# evictor side
def try_evict(page):
    if tenant_manager.is_recovering(page.tenant):
        soft_mark(page)    # let it survive rehydrate for N ms
        backoff_queue.push(page)
    else:
        evict_now(page)

# tenant-manager side
def start_rehydrate(tenant, epoch):
    tenant_state[tenant].recovery_epoch = epoch
    # ephemeral flag with TTL
```
This keeps evictor from nuking pages actively being pulled back by the tenant.

nina: I like low-touch approach, but watch out for race: two nodes could both think tenant is 'recovering' and hoard pages (deadlock) if we don't include epoch/lease semantics. we need a monotonic token so only one recovery window wins for a given page range.

miguel: +1 on epoch/lease. maybe add a tiny lease token returned by tenant-manager that evictor checks:
`lease = tm.acquire_recovery_lease(tenant, range)`
then evictor checks `if lease.valid_for(page.addr)`. keep TTL short (50-200ms) so we don't block long. also add metric evict_holds and evict_backoffs so we can watch regressions.

sam: alternative design: push backpressure earlier at the request router — throttle rehydration concurrent work and avoid bulk warms that collide with eviction. pro: bounding concurrency is simpler. con: increases user-visible latency for requests that trigger cold pages. handshake seems to localize impact.

ashley: agreed. tradeoffs: router admission control reduces load but impacts latency; evictor handshake minimizes user latency at the cost of more complex lifecycle state and potential hoarding if not TTL'd. i think handshake + short TTL + metrics is the best balance for our workload patterns.

nina: test plan requests:
- unit: lease flip when two nodes race (simulate)
- integration: staging canary with handshake enabled for 10% tenants for 48h
- telemetry: new histograms for evict_backoff_duration, rehydrate_latency_p95_by_tenant

miguel: i'll prototype the tm API and a minimal evictor check. can we tighten SLO goal? target is reduce p99 token latency by ~30% during background demotes, and keep extra memory residency < 3% of host memory.

ashley: those targets sound reasonable. i'll draft a brief RFC with API, proto sketches, and rollout plan (canary -> wider). will include sample k8s feature flag and a metric dashboard.

incident-bot: IncidentBot created perf-alert #1234 for p99-token-latency > 2.5s (staging).

sam: nice. once RFC exists i'll review. can we add a fallback: if eviction hold count grows > X, evictor falls back to immediate evict to avoid cross-tenant OOM?

ashley: yes — include a circuit-breaker: if held_pages > threshold or tenant_total_resident > cap then bypass lease checks and prioritize safety. will add that to RFC.

miguel: i'll sync with eng-sre on alert thresholds and help add dashboards.

nina: :thumbsup: please add the race unit tests.

ashley: thanks all — i'll open the RFC and tag @sam @miguel @nina and eng-runtime. planning to run 48h canary in staging next week.

sam: ack
